title: Dialogue
summary: A short everyday dialogue: read and heard, its next lines chosen, one written down.
description: A course's dialogue, practised line by line: the first thing a course's path offers.

requirements.text: A course's dialogue lines make up one dialogue lesson of that course; lines added later join it.
The tutor makes a dialogue only as part of a course, never as a lesson on its own.
A dialogue lesson opens with the whole dialogue to read and hear.
A dialogue of five lines or more asks for two lines what comes next, lines that answer a question first.
The wrong choices for what comes next are lines from far away in the dialogue, never the ones around the gap.
One more line is written down as it is said, in its speaker's voice.
Where speaking cards are on, one of the what-comes-next lines is said aloud instead of chosen.
